answer: Each identity files one claim on a marble board and locks a 70-credit bond. Each epoch a beacon draws pairs: one key behind two conflicting claims proves equivocation and both bonds burn, half to the challenger. Fees rise 7 credits per identity from 36, so 1,000 fakes pay 3,532,500 plus 70,000 locked against a 40,000 pool. A rented umber stamp names its lender, so both burn. An honest agent files once, pays 36, keeps its share.
